properties.name: Kentucky/Tennessee to Ohio
properties.description: After settling Kentucky and Tennessee, many Scotch-Irish families moved north across the Ohio River. Ohio became a state in 1803 and offered good farmland with access to river transportation.

properties.name: Ohio to Indiana
properties.description: Indiana became a state in 1816. Scotch-Irish families continued westward, following the National Road and establishing farms in central Indiana.

properties.name: Indiana to Illinois
properties.description: Illinois became a state in 1818. Families crossed the Wabash River, settling the prairies. This marked the transition from woodland to prairie farming.

properties.name: Kentucky/Tennessee to Missouri
properties.description: Many families moved directly from the Appalachian base to Missouri, which became a state in 1821. The Boone's Lick Trail and Santa Fe Trail brought settlers to Missouri's fertile river valleys.

properties.name: Appalachia to Texas
properties.description: Texas independence (1836) and statehood (1845) attracted Scotch-Irish settlers. Many moved from Tennessee through Arkansas to Texas, bringing Presbyterian traditions to the frontier.

properties.name: Illinois/Missouri to Kansas
properties.description: The Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854) opened Kansas for settlement. Free-state settlers, many of Scotch-Irish descent, moved to Kansas before and after the Civil War.

properties.name: Oregon Trail Migration
properties.description: Some McCreary families joined the great migrations to Oregon and California. The Oregon Trail started in Missouri, and the California Gold Rush (1849) drew many westward.
